precepts.text: The fast the Most High chooses is a day to afflict the soul before him.
precepts.point: Ezra was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help against the enemy in the way, having testified that the hand of God is upon all who seek him for good.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

precepts.why:
Ezra “proclaimed a fast there, at the river of Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before our God.” To afflict the soul is to fast, taking neither food nor water. Isaiah puts the fast and the affliction together: “Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the Lord?”

The fast the Most High chooses is a day to afflict the soul before him. That is what Ezra's company did at Ahava: they afflicted themselves before their God “to seek of him a right way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our substance.” One may fast and pray for wisdom and a right path, as they did.

precepts.text: Lacking wisdom, one may ask of God, who gives liberally, and it shall be given.
precepts.point: Ezra was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help against the enemy in the way, having testified that the hand of God is upon all who seek him for good.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

precepts.why:
Ezra fasted to seek of God “a right way for us.” That is asking for wisdom, and “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.”

Ezra had told the king that “The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him”, and was ashamed to ask for soldiers and horsemen after saying so. So instead of the king's band he sought the Most High by fasting and prayer for a right path for the people, the little ones and their substance. Whoever lacks wisdom may ask the same way, and it shall be given.

points: The chief of the fathers and their genealogy are recorded, listing the heads of families who went up with Ezra from Babylon and the number of males with each.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

points: Every name is set down deliberately. These were actual people who put their work into the building of the house, and names mean something, which is why Israel desires their names written in the book.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

points: Ezra gathered the company at the river Ahava, abode three days, and viewing the people found none of the sons of Levi, so he sent men of understanding to Iddo at Casiphia to bring ministers for the house.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

points: By the good hand of the Most High they brought back men of understanding of the sons of Levi and a large number of Nethinims appointed for the service, all expressed by name. Ezra knew which men among him had understanding and called on them.

note.label: Ezra 8: The Company Returns And Fasts At Ahava

points: Ezra proclaimed a fast at the river Ahava that they might afflict their souls before the Most High and seek of him a right way for themselves, their little ones, and their substance. To afflict the soul is to fast, taking neither food nor water, and one may fast and pray for wisdom and a right path.
